## Setting up the expectation

Let $N$ be the number of games in the match. The match ends at game $n$ when one player reaches 21 wins, so $N$ ranges from 21 to 41. Since the loser can win at most 20 games, $N = 21 + k$ with $0 \le k \le 20$.

Frank wins the match with $n$ games and Joe having $k=n-21$ wins with probability $\binom{20+k}{k}p^{21}q^k$, where $p=0.3$ and $q=0.7$. The symmetric case applies when Joe wins. Using $(21+k)\binom{20+k}{k} = 21\binom{21+k}{k}$:

$$E[N] = 21\sum_{k=0}^{20}\binom{21+k}{k}\left(p^{21}q^k + q^{21}p^k\right)$$

## Rewriting as binomial tails

Since $\sum_{k=0}^{20}\binom{21+k}{k}p^{22}q^k = P(\text{22nd success occurs by trial }42) = P(\text{Bin}(41,p)\ge 22)$, we get

$$E[N] = \frac{21}{p}\,P(\text{Bin}(41,p)\ge 22) + \frac{21}{q}\,P(\text{Bin}(41,q)\ge 22)$$

Also $P(\text{Bin}(41,0.7)\ge 22) = P(\text{Bin}(41,0.3)\le 19)$.

## Computing the tail probabilities

Let $X\sim\text{Bin}(41,0.3)$ and $b(k)=P(X=k)$. Starting from $b(0)=0.7^{41}\approx 4.456764\times10^{-7}$ and using $b(k+1)/b(k) = \frac{3(41-k)}{7(k+1)}$, the upper-tail terms are:

| $k$ | $b(k)$ |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.0052438 |
| 21 | 0.0022474 |
| 22 | 0.0008756 |
| 23 | 0.0003100 |
| 24 | 0.0000997 |
| 25 | 0.0000290 |
| 26 | 0.0000077 |
| 27+ | ≈0.0000023 |

This gives:
- $P(X\ge 22) \approx 0.0013243$
- $P(X\ge 20) \approx 0.0088154$, so $P(X\le 19) \approx 0.9911846$

## Final computation

$$E[N] = \frac{21}{0.3}(0.0013243) + \frac{21}{0.7}(0.9911846) \approx 0.0927 + 29.7355 \approx 29.83$$

As a sanity check, the loser's expected number of wins is about $21\cdot 0.3/0.7 \approx 9$, so a total near 30 is plausible.

ANSWER: ≈ 29.83
